claims.text: The proposed intervention is to add less than 0.5 at.% Y during synthesis of the CoCrFeNiMn bond coat.
Trace Y addition will cause Y to segregate to grain boundaries.
Trace Y addition will cause Y to segregate to the bond-coat/oxide interface.
Segregated Y will form finely dispersed Y-rich oxide particles embedded in the protective oxide scale.
Y-rich oxide particles will stabilize and improve the adhesion of the protective oxide layer.
The reactive-element effect of Y will facilitate rapid formation of a stable alumina or complex-oxide scale.
Y-rich particles will anchor the oxide scale to the substrate.
The proposed Y-mediated mechanism will slow oxide-scale growth kinetics.
The Y-doped bond coat will have a slower oxide-scale growth rate than the untreated bond coat.
The Y-doped bond coat will experience fewer oxide-spallation events than the untreated bond coat.
Trace Y addition will extend bond-coat operational lifespan and improve durability and reliability under cyclic high-temperature oxidation.
Undoped CoCrFeNiMn forms mixed Mn-, Cr-, and Fe-containing oxide scales during high-temperature oxidation in air.
Oxidation of undoped CoCrFeNiMn can produce a spatially nonuniform oxide scale.
Undoped CoCrFeNiMn oxide scales are typically less adherent and prone to spallation during high-temperature cycling.
The Y-induced improvement should remain effective in oxidizing, thermally cycled service up to approximately 1100 °C.
The reactive-element effect is well documented outside the direct CoCrFeNiMn evidence presented here.

contradictions.description: The stated alloy and intervention contain Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, Mn, and trace Y but no Al, while the mechanism invokes formation of a stable alumina scale without specifying any source of aluminum.
